issues.description: Conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock field modifiers: the problem statement first instructs students to declare a final Stock stock and to initialize it in the SealSaloon constructor (per-instance final field, see problem_statement.md lines 70-71), but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static and shared across all instances (see problem_statement.md lines 77-81). The solution implementation declares the field as static final (private static final Stock stock = new Stock(); in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 5). The two instructions conflict because a static final field cannot be initialized in an instance constructor as the statement on lines 70-71 suggests. This contradiction will confuse students about whether stock should be a per-instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static (class) field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement. Option A (preferred if stock must be shared): state that stock is a static final field and must be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (example: private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). Update the earlier paragraph to remove the instruction to initialize stock in the instance constructor. Also clarify that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice should be static because they operate on the shared static stock. Option B (if stock should be per-instance): change the later note that marks stock as static and state instead that stock is a non-static final field that must be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor; also make acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice non-static so they operate on the instance stock. Update the problem statement text to explicitly show the intended modifier and where students should perform initialization so there is no ambiguity.
